name: railsforge
description: All-in-one Ruby on Rails intelligence: Schema Peek, Fast MVC Navigation, Route Autocomplete, RuboCop Autocorrect, Brakeman Security, Service Object Extractors, and @rails AI Agent.

scripts.package: pnpm run lint && pnpm run type-check && pnpm run compile && pnpm test && pnpm run vsce-package

railsForge.excludePatterns.description: Glob patterns excluded from every RailsForge workspace scan (schema/route/pattern indexing, AST index, live re-indexing on save). Set at the workspace level (.vscode/settings.json) to exclude project-specific directories (e.g. a vendored engine's dummy app, a generated docs folder) on top of, or instead of, the defaults. The RailsForge MCP server (run outside VS Code) also reads this from the workspace's .vscode/settings.json.

enumDescriptions: Adds AI request/response summaries, latency, and diff-parse results
Adds raw HTTP request/response payloads sent to the AI provider — these contain your code/prompts, so be careful before sharing logs
railsForge.log.level.description: Verbosity of the RailsForge output channel (View → Output → RailsForge) and the railsForge.log.file mirror. Applies immediately on change — no window reload needed.

railsForge.log.file.description: Mirror every log line to <workspace>/.railsforge/railsforge.log (the .railsforge/ directory is already gitignored). Intended for capturing issues to attach to a bug report; the file grows unbounded, so delete it when you're done.

enumDescriptions: Detect automatically from Gemfile.lock, config/application.rb, ApplicationController, and *.gemspec (default)
Force full Rails MVC treatment (views/helpers/asset pipeline features shown)
Force API-only Rails treatment (views/Hotwire features hidden; schema/routes/models kept)
Force Ruby gem treatment (Rails-specific features hidden; pattern catalog matches lib/**)
Force plain Ruby script treatment (same as gem, minus gem-publishing commands)
railsForge.projectType.override.description: Override RailsForge's auto-detected project type. Controls which commands/keybindings appear (see the Architecture sidebar for what was detected) — set this when auto-detection gets it wrong, e.g. an API-only app without `config.api_only = true` set yet. Requires a window reload to take effect.

railsForge.rubocop.autocorrectOnSave.description: Automatically run RuboCop autocorrect (mode per railsForge.rubocop.mode) on every Ruby file save

railsForge.rubocop.mode.description: RuboCop autocorrect mode used by both the 'RuboCop Autocorrect File' command and rubocop.autocorrectOnSave: safe (-a) or unsafe (-A)

railsForge.brakeman.scanOnSave.description: Run a Brakeman security scan in the background on Ruby file save (Rails projects only). Debounced to at most once every 30s since Brakeman scans the whole project, not just the saved file; silent when clean, shows a notification with a 'Show Report' action when it finds warnings.

railsForge.testing.framework.description: Fallback framework for 'Run Test'/'Debug Test' when a test file's path doesn't unambiguously indicate spec/ (RSpec) or test/ (Minitest)

railsForge.schema.autoIndex.description: Auto-index db/schema.rb on file changes. Requires a window reload to take effect.

railsForge.routes.autoIndex.description: Auto-index config/routes.rb on file changes. Requires a window reload to take effect.

railsForge.ollama.host.description: URL of the local Ollama instance

railsForge.ollama.model.description: Default Ollama model to use for @rails AI Agent

railsForge.ollama.embeddingModel.description: Ollama model used for RailsForge: Semantic Search (must be pulled separately, e.g. `ollama pull nomic-embed-text`). Search falls back to keyword matching if this model or Ollama itself is unavailable.

railsForge.ollama.numCtx.description: Ollama context window (num_ctx) for the @rails agent. Small local models default to ~2048-4096, which truncates RailsForge's system prompt + file content and causes malformed AI fixes; 8192 fits the prompt and diff-format instructions. Raise to 16384 for files over ~200 lines. Only sent to Ollama; ignored for cloud providers.

railsForge.ollama.keepAlive.description: How long the Ollama model stays loaded in memory after a request (keep_alive). Keeps the model resident so AI-fix and chat calls skip the cold-start load. Only sent to Ollama; ignored for cloud providers.

railsForge.ollama.repeatPenalty.description: Ollama repeat penalty for the @rails agent. Suppresses the repetition loops small local models fall into; 1.0 disables it. Only sent to Ollama; ignored for cloud providers.

railsForge.ollama.minP.description: Ollama min_p filter for the @rails agent. Keeps high-probability tokens and drops low-probability noise, improving output quality on small models. Only sent to Ollama; ignored for cloud providers.

enumDescriptions: Cloud — requires an API key set via 'RailsForge: Set AI Provider API Key'
Cloud — requires an API key set via 'RailsForge: Set AI Provider API Key'
VS Code's own model picker (Copilot or any installed Language Model provider, e.g. an Ollama provider) — no API key stored by RailsForge; VS Code asks for consent
railsForge.ai.provider.description: Backend for the @rails AI agent and chat participant. Cloud providers send your code/prompts to that provider's API — only switch away from 'ollama' if you're fine with that. Requires a window reload to take effect.

railsForge.ai.vscodeLm.family.description: Preferred model family (e.g. 'gpt-4o', 'claude-sonnet') when railsForge.ai.provider is 'vscode-lm'. Empty uses the first available model.

railsForge.ai.openai.model.description: OpenAI model used when railsForge.ai.provider is 'openai'

railsForge.ai.openai.baseUrl.description: Base URL for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Point this at OpenRouter, a self-hosted vLLM, or any OSS model gateway (e.g. oss-gpt 120b) that speaks the /v1/chat/completions protocol. The agent appends /v1/chat/completions automatically.

railsForge.ai.anthropic.model.description: Anthropic model used when railsForge.ai.provider is 'anthropic'

railsForge.ai.temperature.description: Sampling temperature for the @rails agent, applied to every provider. 0.2 keeps AI fixes deterministic (good for diff generation); raise toward 1.0 for more creative chat answers.

railsForge.ai.maxTokens.description: Maximum generated tokens per response. Sent as num_predict to Ollama and max_tokens to cloud providers. For a 4B local model this caps rambling and cuts round time; cloud models can handle a larger cap (e.g. 4096).

railsForge.ai.timeoutMs.description: Per-request timeout for @rails agent calls. Prevents a hung or overloaded Ollama/cloud endpoint from blocking a fix or chat turn indefinitely.

railsForge.legal.skills.enabled.description: Enable legal-domain AI guardrails inspired by the lawve-ai/awesome-legal-skills vscode-extension-builder-lawvable skill pack. Adds jurisdiction, confidentiality, citation, uncertainty, and attorney-review guidance to @rails prompts for legal-tech workspaces.

railsForge.mcp.enabled.description: Whether 'RailsForge: Export Cursor Rules & Register MCP Server' also registers the RailsForge MCP server (in .cursor/mcp.json). When false, that command still writes .cursor/rules/railsforge.mdc but skips MCP server registration. The MCP server itself always runs over stdio, started on demand by the MCP client (Cursor/Claude Code) — there is no in-editor 'server process' to start/stop or a port to configure.

railsForge.apiDocs.enabled.description: Whether 'RailsForge: Generate OpenAPI Skeleton' is available. Most useful for API-only projects.

railsForge.performance.cacheSize.description: Maximum entries kept in RailsForge's bounded in-memory caches (Gem Lens gem-info lookups, semantic-search embeddings, APIDock notes) before evicting the least-recently-used entry.

enumDescriptions: Automatically configure VS Code file watcher and search exclusions for large Rails repositories on startup.
Show a prompt asking before configuring workspace performance optimizations.
Do not automatically optimize workspace settings on startup.
railsForge.performance.autoOptimizeWorks.description: How RailsForge optimizes VS Code performance (file watcher and search exclusions) for large Rails repositories.

railsForge.apidock.enabled.description: Append apidock.com's top-rated community note (real-world gotchas/edge cases) to the hover tooltip for known Rails/Ruby/RSpec methods.

railsForge.apidock.baseUrl.description: Base URL used for apidock.com lookups. Override to point at a mirror/internal proxy.

railsForge.apidock.requestTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for an apidock.com hover lookup, in milliseconds. A timed-out or failed request degrades to no APIDock note rather than blocking the hover.

railsForge.apidock.cacheTtlHours.description: How long a fetched APIDock note is cached before being re-fetched, in hours.

railsForge.apidock.customMappings.description: Extra (or overriding) entries for the hovered-word → apidock.com Class/method lookup used by the APIDock hover note. Each entry overrides any built-in mapping with the same keyword.

keyword.description: The bare word to match when hovering, e.g. "has_many"

className.description: apidock.com class/module path, slash-separated for nested modules, e.g. "ActiveRecord/Base"

methodName.description: Method name as it appears in the apidock.com URL

railsForge.devdocs.baseUrl.description: Base URL loaded by 'RailsForge: Open DevDocs'. Override to point at a self-hosted DevDocs instance.

railsForge.devdocs.openBesideActiveEdito.description: Open the DevDocs panel in a column beside the active editor. When false, it opens in the active editor's own column.

railsForge.rubydoc.enabled.description: Whether 'RailsForge: Open Gem Documentation' and the get_gem_documentation MCP tool are available.

railsForge.rubydoc.baseUrl.description: Base URL used for rubydoc.info gem documentation lookups. Override to point at a mirror/internal proxy.

railsForge.rubydoc.requestTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for a rubydoc.info lookup, in milliseconds.

railsForge.rubydoc.cacheTtlDays.description: How long a fetched gem doc entry is cached before being re-fetched, in days. Gem docs are immutable per version, so this can safely be long.

railsForge.devdocs.offlineEnabled.description: Download the project's Ruby/Rails DevDocs docsets to .railsforge/devdocs/ on activation and use them for zero-latency, fully offline hover documentation. When false, only APIDock's network-backed community notes appear on hover.

railsForge.devdocs.dataBaseUrl.description: Base URL DevDocs docset data (index.json/db.json) is downloaded from. Override to point at a mirror/internal proxy.

railsForge.devdocs.fetchTimeoutMs.description: Timeout for downloading a DevDocs docset file, in milliseconds. Each docset is several MB, hence the longer default than APIDock/RubyDoc's per-hover timeouts.

railsForge.devdocs.rubySlug.description: DevDocs docset slug to use for offline Ruby core docs, e.g. "ruby~3.3". Empty: derived from the project's detected Ruby version.

railsForge.devdocs.railsSlug.description: DevDocs docset slug to use for offline Rails docs, e.g. "rails~7.1". Empty: derived from the project's detected Rails version.

railsForge.rubydoc.namespaceMappings.description: Extra (or overriding) entries for the constant-namespace → gem-name lookup used to resolve 'RailsForge: Open Gem Documentation' and get_gem_documentation. Only needed for a gem whose top-level module doesn't match its snake_cased or lowercased gem name.

gem.description: Gem name as it appears in Gemfile.lock, e.g. "view_component"

railsForge.types.steepEnabled.description: Enable Steep type-checker diagnostics ('RailsForge: Run Steep Type Check'). Requires a Steepfile and the steep gem; off by default since most projects don't use RBS/Steep.

railsForge.types.steepScanOnSave.description: Automatically re-run Steep in the background on Ruby file save when railsForge.types.steepEnabled is true. Debounced (like brakeman.scanOnSave) since Steep checks the whole configured target, not just the saved file.

railsForge.analyzers.enabled.description: Analyzers run by 'RailsForge: Run Code Analyzers' (findings go to the Problems panel). They must be in your bundle (bundle add <name> --group development). Empty = ask each time.

railsForge.analyzers.flogThreshold.description: Flog complexity score at or above which a method is reported.

railsForge.runtime.introspection.enabled.markdownDescription: Allow RailsForge to run `rails runner` to read the application's real models, associations, validations, callbacks, routes and middleware. **This boots your app and executes its initializers.** When off, RailsForge asks before each run. Never runs in untrusted workspaces.

railsForge.ruby.versionManager.description: Version manager used to run project tools (RuboCop, Rails, RSpec, Brakeman, ...) so the project's Ruby is used even when VS Code was launched without shell init. 'auto' detects it from .tool-versions / mise.toml / .ruby-version and only wraps when the manager is installed; 'none' runs tools directly.

railsForge.types.rbsSigDir.description: Directory (relative to the workspace root) RBS signature files are read from for hover/go-to-definition, and written to by 'RailsForge: Generate RBS Signatures for File'.

task.description: Preset id (test, rubocop, brakeman, db:migrate, db:rollback, db:prepare, db:seed, routes) or one of rake / rails / rspec / rubocop together with args.

args.description: Arguments for rake / rails / rspec / rubocop tasks (passed as argv, not through a shell).

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_schema
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns database columns for a model (or all tables if no model is given), from db/schema.rb.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_list_routes
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists routes, optionally filtered by a search string matched against verb/path/controller#action.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_list_patterns
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists this project's own Service/Query/Form/Policy/Decorator/Concern classes, optionally filtered by type.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_find_similar_pattern
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Given a proposed class name (e.g. "CreateOrderService"), finds the closest existing Service/Query/etc. in this project — use before generating new code.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_dependencies
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns collaborators (what this class depends on) and callers (what depends on this class), from the persistent AST index. Requires the workspace to have been opened in VS Code with RailsForge at least once.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_find_duplicate_methods
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks the codebase for near-duplicate method bodies (candidates for extracting a shared concern/method) — call this before generating a new method, to avoid writing a redundant duplicate of existing logic. Requires the persistent AST index.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_method_notes
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches apidock.com's community notes and doc summary for a Ruby/Rails/RSpec method — call this before generating code that uses an unfamiliar method, to ground it in real-world gotchas (skipped validations/callbacks, deprecated behavior, surprising defaults) that official docs often miss. This is APIDock only (community notes); for the official signature/description of a Ruby core or Rails framework method, prefer get_offline_docs instead — it's instant (no network call) when the docset is cached.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_gem_documentation
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches YARD documentation (signature, description, params, return type) for a class/method in one of this project's dependency gems, at the exact version locked in Gemfile.lock — use this before generating code that calls into a gem (Pundit, Sidekiq, dry-rb, etc.) whose API isn't in RailsForge's own indexed patterns.

gem_name.description: Gem name as it appears in Gemfile.lock, e.g. "pundit". Omitted: resolved from class_name's top-level namespace.

class_name.description: Class or module name, e.g. "Pundit" or "Sidekiq::Client"

version.description: Exact gem version. Omitted: read from this project's Gemfile.lock.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_offline_docs
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Looks up a Ruby/Rails method or class in this project's locally cached DevDocs data (.railsforge/devdocs/, downloaded by the extension on activation) — instant, no network call, no tokens spent fetching a web page. Prefer this over get_method_notes/get_gem_documentation when you just need the official signature/description for a Ruby core or Rails framework method; use those for community gotchas or gem-specific (non-Rails) APIs instead.

symbol_name.description: Bare method name (e.g. "update_attribute") or class/module name (e.g. "ActiveRecord::Base")

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_rbs_signature
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the RBS (Ruby type signature) declaration for a method, from this project's sig/ directory, if one exists. Use this to check a method's declared parameter/return types before calling it or writing code against it.

class_name.description: Class/module name to disambiguate when the same method name is declared on multiple classes

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_list_rake_tasks
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists this project's Rake tasks (name, namespace, description) via `rake -T` — use before suggesting a shell command, to check whether a task for it already exists (e.g. db:migrate, a custom deploy/report task) rather than proposing a new script.

filter.description: Only return tasks whose name contains this substring

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_suggest_learning_resource
languageModelTools.displayName: Suggest a learning resource for a design smell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Given one of RailsForge's own design-principle diagnostic ids (SRP-FAT-CLASS, DEMETER-VIOLATION, KISS-METAPROGRAMMING, YAGNI-UNUSED-PRIVATE — as seen in this project's "RailsForge Principles" diagnostics), returns a specific book/chapter recommendation for further reading.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Suggest a learning resource for a design smell

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_project_guidelines
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns this project's actual conventions — from .railsforge.yml if the team wrote one, otherwise learned from the codebase's own existing Service Objects (majority base class + entry-point method name, only when the codebase actually agrees on one) — so an AI agent generates a Service Object matching this repo's real pattern (e.g. `Interactor`/`run`) instead of assuming the generic Rails-generator default (`ApplicationService`/`call`). Call this before generating a new Service Object.

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_example_file
languageModelTools.displayName: Get a representative example file for a pattern type
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the full content of this project's most complete existing Service/Query/Form/Policy/Decorator/Concern, so an AI agent can learn the repo's real style (naming, error handling, how it structures the class) by example instead of guessing. Call this alongside get_project_guidelines before generating a new file of the same pattern type.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Get a representative example file for a pattern type

languageModelTools.name: railsforge_get_runtime_introspection
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns what the RUNNING Rails app knows — real ActiveRecord associations, validations, callbacks, routes and middleware — from the cached `rails runner` snapshot (.railsforge/runtime.json). More accurate than static parsing for metaprogrammed models. Only available after the developer ran "RailsForge: Refresh Rails Runtime Introspection" (it boots the app, so it is never run automatically).

model.description: Only this model (e.g. "User"); omitted: a summary of every model plus routes
